column1: # nexus-f3yqd.2.19 (RDR-246): one verification text per row, the verdict BOTH the registration gate and the data-move worker must give.
# Read by DataMoveVerificationParityRulesTest (gate: DataMoveChangesetRules.refusesVerification, the blank check and badPlaceholders)
# and by MoveSqlParityIntegrationTest (worker: MoveSql.countRows on a real server).
#   accept       the gate lets it register, the worker runs it.
#   refuse       the gate refuses it, the worker throws MoveSql.Refused (its own rule or the bind-count check).
#   refuse-loud:SQLSTATE  the gate refuses it, the worker does not run it either, but no worker rule says so: the server rejects it
#                (a SQLException) with that SQLSTATE, and the state must be one the failure classifier calls permanent. The rows are
#                text that is not SQL at all (adjacent dollar quotes, an E-string at the start, an e' after a quote, a $, a backslash
#                or a non-ASCII letter) and E-strings the driver ends early (a doubled quote then an escaped one). A row moves to
#                refuse when the worker gets a rule for it.
# A row is valid PostgreSQL unless it is refuse-loud: a lexer difference on text the server rejects is the server's to report.
# Format: verdict TAB name TAB text. In text: \\ is a backslash, \n a newline, \r a carriage return, \t a tab, {VTAB} a one-row
# derived table (the @vtab line below), so an accept row is real SQL the worker's test runs on a server.
